content: Brompheniramine is an antihistamine that is prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as red, irritated, itchy, watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny nose caused by allergies, hay fever, or the common cold. It may also help relieve itching from insect bites, bee stings, poison ivy, and poison oak. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in the form of regular tablets, extended-release (long-acting) tablets, and liquid, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken every 4, 6, 8, or 12 hours as needed. Follow the instructions on the package label or your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take brompheniramine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor or the package label. Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush, break, or chew them. Do not give extended-release tablets to children under 12 years of age, and do not give regular tablets or oral liquid to children under 6 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Before taking brompheniramine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to brompheniramine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other medications for colds, hay fever, or allergies; medications for depression or seizures; muscle relaxants; narcotics (pain medications); sedatives; sleeping pills; tranquilizers; and vitamins. Do not take brompheniramine if you have taken an MAO inhibitor within the past two weeks. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, diabetes, glaucoma, ulcers, difficulty urinating (due to an enlarged prostate gland), heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, or an overactive thyroid gland. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking brompheniramine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking brompheniramine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Brompheniramine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, nose, and throat, upset stomach, headache, chest congestion, and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include vision problems, difficulty urinating, muscle weakness, unusual excitement (especially in children), prolonged drowsiness, dizziness, and skin rash. If you experience any of these severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
